ai.title: SDK stops retrying final session and spend refusals
ai.summary: The SDK model provider now treats intentional server refusals, specifically the per-turn spend breaker and superseded session errors, as final by throwing a non-retryable `APICallError` on the first response. The previous logic only handled the 429 spend limit, but now a new `FINAL_REFUSALS` table checks the response status and error code to bypass the AI SDK's default retry loop for these specific failures. This change ensures that the user-facing error message from the server is preserved and not masked by generic rate-limit or conflict retry noise.

eli5.text: When the service deliberately refuses a request because you hit a spending cap or because your session was already started elsewhere, the software now stops immediately instead of quietly waiting and trying again up to four times. This applies to anyone using the free coding assistant in their terminal, on the web, or on their desktop.
